headline: Red session on Hormuz/oil fears: KSE-100 opened firm (intraday high 175,354) but sold off through the afternoon to close 173,636 (-1,693pts, -0.97%) as US-Iran tensions and Brent near $98 stoked inflation/external-account worries — banks and E&Ps (UBL, OGDC, PPL, MCB, FFC) did most of the damage; none of those are portfolio holdings, which is why the book barely moved. Portfolio value ~Rs 10.16M, P/L +Rs 112K (+1.12% on cost), down slightly from Friday's +1.53% mostly on CPHL (-4.6% since Fri, no company news — general pharma softness). No holding moved >5% since the last review, so no notification triggered. Drawdown from the Jan ATH is now ~8.4% (up from ~7.6% Friday) — still short of the 10% dry-powder trigger but closing in faster than usual given today's move. AVN's EXIT call remains unexecuted (24,500 shares still held, 9 reviews running) — no new company news. DRAP pricing-formula story escalated a notch: the Economic Affairs minister has now directed DRAP to urgently revise the framework (was 'under consideration', now an active directive), industry still opposing — GLAXO/SEARL stance unchanged (HOLD, watch into Q4). Housekeeping: git connectivity to github.com timed out earlier in this run (raw.githubusercontent.com/api.github.com stayed reachable throughout, so it was isolated to the git endpoint) but recovered before this review finished — Friday's Sep 4 update, which had been stuck unpushed since that review, went out together with this one; the site is fully current again.
market: KSE-100 closed 173,636.07 Mon Sep 7, down 1,692.75pts (-0.97%) after an early rally to 175,353.67 faded under afternoon selling. Drivers: renewed US-Iran tensions over the Strait of Hormuz (Iran has said it will declare a new restricted zone and shipping corridor there) pushed Brent crude near a 7-week high (~$98), stoking Pakistan's import-bill/current-account worries; separately, news that government plans financial penalties on refineries missing an Oct 1 upgrade deadline hit PRL (-10%). UBL/OGDC/PPL/MCB/FFC alone cost the index ~811pts — none are portfolio holdings. Drawdown from the Jan 23 ATH (189,556) is now ~8.4%, up from ~7.6% Friday — still below the 10% line that would justify shifting the AICF/MICF cash reserve into MZNPETF/MIIETF, but the gap narrowed meaningfully in one session; worth watching daily if Hormuz tensions keep escalating. SBP holds at 11.5%; next MPC meeting is Sep 14, 2026 (no change expected, but flagging the date). SBP reserves rose to $17.12B (week of Aug 28), external-accounts picture still constructive despite the oil-price worry. DRAP drug-pricing review: escalated from 'under consideration' to the Economic Affairs minister directing DRAP to urgently revise the pricing formula, Hardship Policy and Policy Board composition (adding a health economist and public-health expert); pharma industry associations continue to publicly oppose. Nothing enacted yet — still a sector-wide watch item, not a GLAXO/SEARL-specific fundamental break; HOLD stance unchanged for both, watch into Q4. EFERT — no material news since the Q2 briefing; the Rs2/share interim dividend some data providers list against a Sep 3 pay date is actually the same interim credited back on May 13, 2026 (stale/duplicated record on third-party sites) — no new dividend event, WATCH/re-evaluate-at-Q3 stance unchanged. AVN — no new company announcements; EXIT call unexecuted through 9 reviews now. CPHL was the biggest single-name mover this review, down ~4.6% since Friday (Rs76.18 → Rs72.68) with no company-specific news found — reads as general pharma-sector softness riding alongside the DRAP overhang rather than anything CPHL-specific; not enough to change the HOLD. DATA QUALITY: stock prices refreshed normally (as of ~15:01 UTC / 20:01 PKT close). Fund NAVs (funds_updated: Aug 13) are now 25 days stale — the MUFAP scraper issue remains unresolved; ~30% of portfolio value (all 7 funds) is still being priced off a nearly month-old NAV snapshot, a growing blind spot needing a real fix.

actions.title: Avanceon — thesis still broken, EXIT call unexecuted through 9 reviews
actions.detail: No new news since the Aug 28 H1/Q2 FY26 filing: consolidated H1 2026 revenue grew +34% YoY but the company swung from a Rs 168M profit to a Rs 260M NET LOSS (EPS -Rs 0.62 vs +Rs 0.38); Q2 alone the loss widened to Rs 317M. No dividend declared. Admin/selling expenses up 45% YoY outpaced revenue growth, and a one-off 'other income' cushion from last year (Rs 162M) collapsed to Rs 77M this year, exposing weak core operating economics — real, board-confirmed deterioration, not a rumor. Now Rs 29.99, -33.5% on cost. No earnings catalyst pending before Q3; there's no reason left to keep waiting. The Aug 25 EXIT call is unexecuted through 9 reviews now — recommend selling the entire position at market.

entries.basis: Monthly-timeframe accumulation zones for a 10-25yr horizon: where fundamentals + monthly support align to add in small portions. 'entry' = start nibbling at/below; 'add' = deeper monthly support to load more. Pakistan macro-aware (SBP 11.5%, KSE-100 off the Jan ATH). These are accumulation guides, not precise buy/sell signals — verify with your broker.

MZNPETF.note: Broad Islamic index ETF — your #1 DCA vehicle. Accumulate on any dip; entry is just under fair value, add = deeper monthly support.

MIIETF.note: Second index-ETF leg. Same DCA logic — buy small and often, more at the add level.
